spotify.$comment: releasedDate is the publication date of the pinned Windows build (1.2.93.667). Community assets reviewed before it are treated as stale by Build-Scripts.ps1 -Validate. embeddedChromium is the browser engine that build ships, read from libcef.dll on 2026-09-04; pinning Spotify pins that engine, and CEF does not backport Chromium security fixes, so it only moves when the tuple moves.

spicetifyCli.$comment: windowsMinSpotify and windowsDeclaredMaxSpotify are the range the pinned release declares for Windows and Microsoft Store, read off https://github.com/spicetify/cli/releases/tag/v2.44.0. libreSpotVerifiedMaxSpotify is the newest Spotify build LibreSpot has checked against this whole pin set; it is LibreSpot's own ceiling and is never reported as Spicetify's.

routeWiring.$comment: Spotify builds where Repair-SpicetifyCustomAppWiring was run against a real extracted xpui bundle rather than a synthetic fixture. Every build the README names for route re-wiring must appear in verified, and Build-Scripts.ps1 -Validate fails otherwise. To re-run the proof, point LIBRESPOT_XPUI_FIXTURES at a directory holding <build>/xpui/ copies (index.html, the pre-repair xpui.js, and the spicetify-routes-*.js chunks); the bundles are Spotify's and stay outside the repository, so the Pester tests skip when the variable is unset. anchors are the five injection points the repair needs in the live bundle.

verified.evidence: Repairing the pre-repair SpotX bundle (xpui.js.librespot.bak, SHA256 83d804a4...) reproduced the live repaired xpui.js byte for byte. All five anchors matched and the second pass reported Wired without writing. The two hashes are what identify the fixture: a hand-written stand-in cannot match them, so the Pester proof refuses anything that is not the bundle this entry was recorded against.
